title: US 2.0: What We Have In Common

sentences.en: In 1980, Ronald Reagan became President of the United States.
sentences.zh: 1980年，罗纳德·里根当选美国总统。

sentences.en: He quickly raised the temperature of the Cold War
sentences.zh: 他迅速升温了冷战局势

sentences.en: and assumed a muscular stance toward the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 并对苏联采取了强硬姿态。

sentences.en: Let us be aware that while they preach the supremacy of the state,
sentences.zh: 我们要认识到，当他们宣扬国家至上时，

sentences.en: they are the focus of evil in the modern world.
sentences.zh: 他们就是现代世界的邪恶核心。

sentences.en: That September, a message flashed in a secret bunker at Soprakow 15,
sentences.zh: 当年9月，在一处名为苏普拉科夫15号的秘密掩体中，一条消息闪烁而至，

sentences.en: a secret Soviet outpost that analyzed satellite data from the United States.
sentences.zh: 这是一个负责分析美国卫星数据的苏联秘密前哨站。

sentences.en: Inside the bunker was a 44-year-old Soviet lieutenant colonel named Stanislav Petrov.
sentences.zh: 掩体内坐着一位44岁的苏联中校，名叫斯坦尼斯拉夫·彼得罗夫。

sentences.en: The military commander saw a button pulsing red.
sentences.zh: 这位军事指挥官看到一个按钮在闪烁红光。

sentences.en: His panel told him the unimaginable had happened.
sentences.zh: 他的控制面板告诉他，难以想象的事情发生了。

sentences.en: The United States had launched a ballistic missile.
sentences.zh: 美国发射了一枚弹道导弹。

sentences.en: Within minutes, the satellite data showed four more missiles had been launched.
sentences.zh: 几分钟内，卫星数据显示又有四枚导弹被发射。

sentences.en: It looked like the United States was trying to cripple the Soviet Union
sentences.zh: 这看起来像是美国企图瘫痪苏联

sentences.en: with a sudden, deadly nuclear attack.
sentences.zh: 并发动突然的、致命的核打击。

sentences.en: There were only seconds for the Soviets to launch strikes in response.
sentences.zh: 苏联只有几秒钟的时间来发射反击导弹。

sentences.en: Stanislav Petrov debated whether to report the attack.
sentences.zh: 斯坦尼斯拉夫·彼得罗夫在犹豫是否要报告这次袭击。

sentences.en: If he did, it could have triggered a massive Soviet response.
sentences.zh: 如果他这样做了，可能会引发苏联的大规模反击。

sentences.en: The Soviet commander did not do what was expected of him.
sentences.zh: 这位苏联指挥官没有做人们预料他会做的事。

sentences.en: He decided the satellite data was wrong and did not report the missiles.
sentences.zh: 他断定卫星数据是错误的，并没有报告这些导弹。

sentences.en: The satellite signals were reflections of sunlight off clouds.
sentences.zh: 卫星信号其实是阳光在云层上的反射。

sentences.en: You probably have never heard of Stanislav Petrov,
sentences.zh: 你可能从未听说过斯坦尼斯拉夫·彼得罗夫，

sentences.en: but you might owe your life to him.
sentences.zh: 但你可能因他而捡回了一条命。

sentences.en: Retaliatory strikes could easily have killed half the populations of both countries.
sentences.zh: 报复性打击本可以轻易消灭两国一半以上的人口。

sentences.en: Researchers have estimated that the nuclear winter that followed
sentences.zh: 研究人员估计，随之而来的核冬天

sentences.en: could have killed 2 billion people worldwide.
There is a lesson in the story about whether fallible human beings
sentences.zh: 这个故事给我们的启示是，容易犯错的人类

sentences.en: should ever have nuclear weapons at their disposal.
sentences.zh: 是否应该掌握核武器这一生死权力。

sentences.en: But our focus today is on a psychological idea.
sentences.zh: 但我们今天的重点是一个心理学概念。

sentences.en: How our minds work when we are under attack.
sentences.zh: 当我们在遭受攻击时，大脑是如何运作的。

sentences.en: It's also the start of a series we're calling
sentences.zh: 这也是我们新系列的开篇，

sentences.en: As we begin what promises to be a pivotal and contentious election season
sentences.zh: 随着美国以及全球许多国家迎来

sentences.en: in the United States and many countries around the world,
sentences.zh: 注定关键且充满争议的选举季，

sentences.en: we're taking a close look at how we engage with our opponents.
sentences.zh: 我们正在密切关注我们如何与反对者打交道。

sentences.en: Over the next few weeks, we'll explore the assumptions we make about our allies and our foes.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几周里，我们将探讨我们对盟友和对手的种种假设。

sentences.en: We'll look to history for lessons.
sentences.zh: 我们将从历史中寻找启示。

sentences.en: And we'll offer specific strategies to engage constructively with our opponents,
sentences.zh: 我们还将提供具体的策略，以便与对手进行建设性的互动，

sentences.en: whether in the political realm, at the dinner table, or at work.
sentences.zh: 无论是在政治领域、餐桌上还是在工作中。

sentences.en: We begin with the psychology of threat, this week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》将从威胁心理学开始讲起。

sentences.en: When something bad happens, it's human nature to look for someone to blame.
sentences.zh: 当坏事发生时，寻找替罪羊是人的本性。

sentences.en: Needless to say, that person usually isn't us.
sentences.zh: 不用说，那个人通常不是我们自己。

sentences.en: The tendency to see others as villains and to cast ourselves as innocent victims
sentences.zh: 把别人视为恶人、把自己包装成无辜受害者的倾向
会在人际关系中造成伤害。

sentences.en: It may also lie beneath some of our deepest societal divides.
sentences.zh: 它也可能是我们社会最深层裂痕的根源所在。

sentences.en: At the University of North Carolina,

sentences.zh: 心理学家兼神经科学家库尔特·格雷

sentences.en: studies what happens in our minds when we think about our political opponents.
sentences.zh: 研究当我们想到政治对手时，我们的大脑会发生什么。

sentences.en: Kurt Gray, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 库尔特·格雷，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thanks so much for having me on.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来参加节目。

sentences.en: Kurt, I want to start our conversation with a story that is very far away from politics,
sentences.zh: 库尔特，我想从一个与政治相去甚远的故事开始我们的谈话，

sentences.en: but I think it has a deep connection with politics at a psychological level.
sentences.zh: 但我认为它在心理层面上与政治有着深厚的联系。

sentences.en: When you were a teenager, you used to drive around with a bunch of high school friends.
sentences.zh: 当你还是个青少年的时候，你经常和一群高中朋友开车到处兜风。

sentences.en: I understand your car was nicknamed Fireball.
sentences.zh: 我听说你的车绰号叫“火球”。

sentences.en: Does that say something about how fast you used to drive?
sentences.zh: 这说明你以前开车开得很快吗？

sentences.en: I used to drive a two-door Pontiac Grand Am.
sentences.zh: 我以前开的是一辆双门庞蒂亚克大阿姆。

sentences.en: It wasn't a flashy car, but I liked to drive it very fast and didn't always pay attention.
sentences.zh: 它不是什么显眼的跑车，但我喜欢开得很快，而且并不总是全神贯注。

sentences.en: So one time you and your friends were heading to a movie
sentences.zh: 所以有一次你和朋友们正去看电影的路上，

sentences.en: when something fairly dramatic happened to you.
sentences.zh: 发生了一件相当戏剧性的事。

sentences.en: Tell me the story of what happened.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲当时发生了什么。

sentences.en: I was 16, had just got my license,
sentences.zh: 我当时16岁，刚拿到驾照不久，

sentences.en: and we were driving in the night to go see a movie,
sentences.zh: 我们在夜里开车去看电影，

sentences.en: And so the streets were, you know, shining in the orange sodium lights,
sentences.zh: 所以街道上，你知道的，闪烁着橙色的钠灯光，

sentences.en: and we were roaring up the road
because the movie started in five minutes and we were ten minutes away.
sentences.zh: 因为电影还有五分钟开场，而我们还要开十分钟才能到。

sentences.en: And I was in the right-hand lane.
There was a lane to my left.
And my friend and shotgun all of a sudden said,
sentences.zh: 坐在副驾驶座上的朋友突然说：

sentences.en: Kurt, you're going to miss the turn.
And so I hauled on the steering wheel to the left.
sentences.zh: 于是我猛地向左打方向盘。

sentences.en: I didn't look in the lane next to me
sentences.zh: 我没有看旁边车道一眼，

sentences.en: because I had to cross the lane to be able to turn left.
sentences.zh: 因为我必须横跨那个车道才能左转。

sentences.en: And there was a car driving next to me.
sentences.zh: 结果旁边刚好有一辆车在开。

sentences.en: And so as I turned, this car slammed on its brakes.
sentences.zh: 当我转弯时，那辆车猛踩刹车。

sentences.en: I suddenly became aware it was there.
sentences.zh: 我突然意识到它的存在。
我们发出了刺耳的摩擦声和尖叫声。

sentences.en: The roads were wet, you know.
And so we spun around in the intersection.
sentences.zh: 我们在十字路口旋转了起来。

sentences.en: I didn't hit it, this other car.
sentences.zh: 我没有撞到它，这辆别的车。

sentences.en: It didn't hit me, and we didn't hit anything else.
sentences.zh: 它没有撞我，我们也没撞到其他任何东西。
所以幸运的是，大家都安然无恙。

sentences.en: We ended up stopped in the wrong direction
sentences.zh: 我们最终在马路对面的错误方向停了下来，

sentences.en: on the other side of the road,
just kind of in a desolate night.
sentences.zh: 就在这样一个荒凉的夜晚里。

sentences.en: I mean, it's still a heart-stopping moment, though,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这仍然是一个让人心跳骤停的时刻，

sentences.en: because I think in that instant,
everyone must have seen how close they came to a crash.
sentences.zh: 每个人都意识到了自己离撞车有多近。

sentences.en: It was terrifying, and it happened so faSt.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了，而且发生得太快了。

sentences.en: I mean, the music was so loud, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，音乐声音那么大，对吧？

sentences.en: We were kind of wrapped in our own world.
sentences.zh: 我们仿佛沉浸在自己的世界里。

sentences.en: And so I opened my window to start to apologize

sentences.en: to the driver of the other car.

sentences.zh: 那是一辆银色的梅赛德斯-奔驰。

sentences.en: And this driver, this guy gets out of the car.
sentences.zh: 然后这个司机，这家伙从车里出来了。

sentences.en: He was in his early 20s, had pretty nice clothes on.
sentences.zh: 他二十出头，穿着挺不错的衣服。

sentences.en: I remember he had curly hair.
He had some silver chains on.
And I just started opening my mouth to say sorry.
sentences.zh: 我正张开嘴准备说对不起。

sentences.en: And he, you know, looks at me, just daggers, right,
